policy_title: Champion Disabled People's Rights and Ban Conversion Practices
stated: Labour is committed to championing the rights of disabled people, introducing the full right to equal pay and disability pay gap reporting for large employers. They will support disabled people into work by improving employment support, access to reasonable adjustments, and tackling the Access to Work backlog, allowing job trials without immediate benefit reassessment. Labour will also make all existing strands of hate crime an aggravated offence and deliver a full trans-inclusive ban on conversion practices, while reforming gender recognition law to a modern process, retaining diagnosis from a specialist doctor.

source.quote: Labour is committed to championing the rights of disabled people and to the principle of working with them, so that their views and voices will be at the heart of all we do. We will introduce the full right to equal pay for disabled people. Building on gender pay gap reporting, we will introduce disability and ethnicity pay gap reporting for large employers. We will support disabled people to work by improving employment support and access to reasonable adjustments. We will also tackle the Access to Work backlog and make sure people can try out a job without fear of an immediate benefit reassessment if it does not work out. Delivering opportunities for all means that everyone should be treated with respect and dignity. Labour will protect LGBT+ and disabled people by making all existing strands of hate crime an aggravated offence. So-called conversion therapy is abuse – there is no other word for it – so Labour will finally deliver a full trans-inclusive ban on conversion practices, while protecting the freedom for people to explore their sexual orientation and gender identity. We will also modernise, simplify, and reform the intrusive and outdated gender recognition law to a new process. We will remove indignities for trans people who deserve recognition and acceptance; whilst retaining the need for a diagnosis of gender dysphoria from a specialist doctor, enabling access to the healthcare pathway. Labour is proud of our Equality Act and the rights and protections it affords women; we will continue to support the implementation of its single-sex exceptions.

bearing_set.reason: Disability pay gap reporting, equal pay rights, improved employment support, Access to Work backlog clearance, and job trials without benefit reassessment all directly affect pay levels and employment security for disabled people.

Making all existing hate crime strands an aggravated offence is a criminal sentencing/justice measure that directly affects victim protection and court outcomes — a criminal justice measure belonging here, not in rights.

The trans-inclusive conversion practices ban and gender recognition law reform are squarely within O9's scope (equal treatment, civil/legal rights for LGBTQ+ people); the equal pay right for disabled people is also an anti-discrimination legal protection.

A conversion practices ban restricts what practitioners (including religious/pastoral counsellors) may offer and what adults may seek; the mechanism is concrete (criminalising certain counselling practices → restricts freedom of practitioners and arguably individual choice to seek certain support), and the net liberty effect is genuinely contested even where it also protects bodily autonomy of those subjected to coercive practices.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: O4 (disabled workers' pay and employment quality), O9 (anti-discrimination, minority protections, equal treatment across disability and gender identity), and O10 (conversion practices ban creates a real, contested liberty effect on practitioners and individual choice, distinct from its equal-treatment justification on O9).
